Now coming to the food, which is the other big reason I keep returning. It never disappoints. Honestly, you could close your eyes, point at anything on the menu, and you will still end up with something delicious. Every dish is consistently well made and full of flavour.

Café Bae – Lower Parel: A Familiar Spot That’s Seen Some Change

I’ve been visiting Café Bae in Lower Parel for the past three years, and over time, I’ve tried pretty much everything on their menu. It’s been a go-to spot for casual meals, and while the food has always been decent, there have been a few changes worth noting.

Earlier, Café Bae felt like a solid pocket-friendly option – good food at fair prices. But lately, the prices have gone up, and with that, the overall value feels a bit off. The space is quite compact and tends to get crowded, which can make the experience feel a bit cramped, especially during peak hours.

That said, some of their food items still stand out. The pizzas are consistently good, and the nachos are definitely worth ordering. The fries are alright – nothing extraordinary, but they do the job. As for the drinks, they’re okay – decent enough, but not a highlight.

Overall, Café Bae still holds some charm, especially if you're familiar with it like I am. Just be prepared for a slightly tighter space and higher prices than before.

featured_reviews.review_text:
If South Mumbai’s cafe culture had to be summed up in one place, this would be it. Cafe Free India brings together great food, a lively setting, and an atmosphere that keeps you hooked from the moment you walk in.

The space carries a strong Goan inspired vibe, paired with an energy that feels vibrant and effortless. What truly sets it apart is the 📍Live Karaoke hosted Four Times a week ( Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun, 9pm onwards ) It adds a sense of excitement to the entire experience and makes the place feel dynamic and interactive.

The food here leans towards indulgent comfort. The parmesan corn ribs are juicy and full of flavour, while the honey chilli lotus root stands out with the perfect balance of sweet and spice. Their pizzas are rich, cheesy, and consistently satisfying.

The drinks menu keeps things interesting with beers on tap and cocktails inspired by iconic parts of Mumbai like the Sea Link. Seasonal additions like the mango chilli margarita bring in a refreshing twist.

When it comes to desserts, this is where you should absolutely give in. The gooey brownie with vanilla ice cream paired with an irresistible mango cream is easily one of the highlights and something you cannot go wrong with.

Overall, Cafe Free India in Lower Parel delivers more than just a meal. With its food, drinks, and high energy karaoke nights, it is a place that promises a fun and memorable outing.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited saz cafe yesterday for lunch and I must say that one of the best American food spread you can have in Mumbai is at Saz. First up talking about the ambience it's just wow and has pretty insta worthy corners. They have this open kitchen which looks good too. It's cited right next to Kamala Mill which makes it easier to locate too.
Coming to the f&b part , we had hibiscus cooler and cucumber mint in mocktails. Both of which were super refreshing and had tonic water top up. Well presented too I must say.
In appetizers we had saz fried chicken as it was recommended by the manager and yes it was simply outstanding. Crisp coated crunchy from outside and tender chicken inside. The dip served with it really went well with it. Also had juicy chicken burger which was for real juicy. You cannot skip on this one if you are burger fan! To my surprise they do have good number of Asian food options like Sushi, dimsums and bao. We decided to give a shot to Chicken teriyaki bao which was this tangy and spicy chicken stuffed inside super soft and fresh baos.
Saz cafe has real good spread of Pizza offerings in their menu and we couldn't resist getting one. Pizza verdure with some smoked chicken add on was our order. Served to us fresh and hot in no time this pizza was loaded with toppings. The crust was soft and tasted really good.
To sum it up all , in desserts we had their signature dessert i.e The Saz brookie which is basically semi gooey chocolate brownie served on hot pan topped up with sea salt caramel ice cream along with some caramel popcorn on top. The hospitality here is pretty good and the kitchen staff makes sure that your food is prepared in no time.
Lower parel indeed have got one of the best American food place and we totally loved it!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Stand By Coffee, Worli on a Sunday after a lovely walk at the Coastal Road promenade, but the experience completely spoiled the mood. The café was in a rush hour, which we understood, but the service was extremely slow and unorganized. We ordered a green tea and a toast and sat right in front of the counter. Even after repeatedly reminding the counter boy and the chef—who were right in front of us—nothing was prepared on time. The toast came after 25 minutes, and the green tea arrived 20 minutes later, only when we got frustrated and asked them to either make it immediately or refund us. By then, the toast had already gone cold.

Another disappointing part was that while placing the order, they didn’t inform us that service charge would be added. Only after paying did we notice it on the bill. We didn’t say anything at that moment because who wants to run back for a small amount while trying to enjoy the day—but the experience that followed made it feel unfair.

When we finally gave our feedback, the staff (possibly the owner) responded casually with just a “thanks for the feedback” and showed no concern. Because of the poor service and attitude, we asked them to remove the ₹30 service charge—not for the amount, but because the service truly didn’t justify it.

I don’t recommend visiting this café on Sundays, and based on this experience, I’m unsure about other days too. This visit really ruined what could have been a great end to a beautiful walk.

Stepping into Café by St. Regis during the autumn season feels like entering a world where time slows down just enough for you to savor it. The soft amber lighting and warm wood accents mirror the hues of the season outside, creating an atmosphere that feels both elegant and inviting. Subtle notes of spice—cinnamon, nutmeg, perhaps even a whisper of roasted chestnut—float through the air, hinting at what the kitchen has prepared.
The special autumn menu is the star of the evening, a celebration of comfort elevated to luxury. Each dish arrives like a small story of the season: vibrant, warm, and thoughtfully composed.
The meal might begin with a velvety roasted pumpkin soup, poured tableside into a bowl dotted with toasted seeds and a swirl of infused cream. Its aroma alone feels like a warm wool scarf wrapped around your senses. A pear and endive salad follows, crisp and refreshing, with just the right touch of autumn sweetness from caramelized walnuts or a drizzle of honey vinaigrette.
And then the main course—perhaps a slow-braised short rib, meltingly tender, resting on truffle-infused parsnip puree. Or a perfectly seared salmon paired with maple-roasted root vegetables. Each bite is a reminder of the season’s depth: hearty, earthy, and quietly luxurious.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Great Spot for an Unbeatable Cup of Chai and Quick Munchies

If you're looking for a solid place to grab a classic cutting chai or a quick evening snack in Parel, Chaos Control Cafe is a fantastic choice. Located right in the thick of the action, this spot has become immensely famous among the younger crowd, college students, and office folks looking to unwind. The vibe here is always energetic and buzzing.
The absolute star of the show here is their tea. They serve an amazing, deeply flavorful Kolkata-style chai in traditional clay kulhads that hits the spot every single time. Paired with their unique snack options like the Varanasi Toast or Bun Maska, it makes for a perfect, pocket-friendly evening ritual. However, a quick word of advice: if you are a hard-core coffee lover, this might not be the place for you. Their coffee simply doesn't match up to the brilliant standards of their chai, so it's best to stick to the tea menu.
As for the ambiance, it's a very small outlet, so indoor sitting is highly limited. In true Mumbai fashion, they have cleverly converted the adjacent side street into an open-air sitting area. It is a prime example of a typical, resourceful Mumbai jugad—sitting under the open sky amidst the city's chaotic energy. While it might not offer a premium, air-conditioned cafe experience, it completely works for a casual hangout with friends.
Overall, for a great cup of tea, tasty quick bites, and a lively neighbourhood atmosphere, it's highly recommended. Just skip the coffee and enjoy the street-side vibe!
